title: UHC native-LAN hardware-control client catalog
selection_basis: Practical twelve-family implementation shortlist, not a measured market-share ranking; Denon/Marantz included as the known baseline.
interpretation: Features describe upstream-evidenced prospective UHC support, not functionality implemented or tested in UHC by this research.
A supported family is not a promise for every model, firmware, zone, source or operating mode.
A missing feature/discovery mechanism means not established in the selected path, not necessarily impossible.
HA pins are observed development-branch requirements, not a proposed lockfile or a claim that PyPI latest is identical.
Licenses are project-level findings; inspect exact files and transitive dependencies before vendoring.

recommended_sequence: Use Denon/Marantz as baseline; exploit existing knowledge rather than replacing it.
First additions: WiiM, MusicCast, BluOS and StreamMagic for broader local control coverage.
Focused amplifier additions: Hegel and Lyngdorf.
Add Onkyo after settling the GPL reuse route; add Sonos when grouping/topology is in scope.
Model-specific follow-ons: Anthem, Arcam and Trinnov, with real-device transcripts.
validation_plan: Create fixture transcripts for discovery, identity, capability negotiation, commands, notifications, errors and reconnect.
Tag evidence as implementation-derived, vendor-spec-verified or hardware-verified; do not turn source-derived support into a hardware-tested claim.
Test packet fragmentation, combined replies, stale and out-of-order events, interrupted connections and reboot.
Test volume min/max/step, fixed output, mute, source changes and zone separation without sending unsafe default levels.
One device connection owner inside UHC; frontends consume UHC state rather than opening competing device sessions.
Keep UHC music providers separate from hardware input/volume ownership.
